20.1.6 The table is a lineage control, not a new reform programme. Chapter 20 tests whether selected Chapter 18 obligations can be represented accurately and safely; it does not displace the diagnosis, legal vehicle, institutional owner, reasons or remedy already identified.

20.2 Law as Code, Rules as Code and the authority boundary

20.2.1 “Law as Code” and “Rules as Code” are useful only if their meanings are separated. Law as Code is the broader inquiry into how legal norms may be represented, tested or implemented computationally, and how code itself structures conduct. Rules as Code is a public-administration method: selected rules are expressed in machine-consumable form through a multidisciplinary process connected to policy and legislative drafting. Neither phrase establishes that software is law.

20.2.2 Four artefacts may coexist.

Table 20.2 — Four artefacts in the computational legal hierarchy

ArtefactWhat it doesWhat it cannot prove
authenticated human-readable instrumentstates the enacted or validly made rule in its authoritative formthat an administrative or software implementation is correct
structured legal representationidentifies provisions, definitions, amendments, relationships and metadatathat every provision is reducible to determinate logic
executable modelapplies declared conditions, calculations or routes to supplied inputslegal truth of contested inputs, institutional competence or lawful exercise of discretion
service implementationcollects evidence, calls the model, records action and communicates with a userauthority beyond the governing law or immunity from reasons, review and remedy

20.2.3 The OECD’s 2020 working paper describes Rules as Code as an official machine-consumable version produced alongside human-readable rules, and treats it as a change in rulemaking rather than a software project; it records limitations and competing conceptions rather than one mature global standard.457 New Zealand’s Better Rules discovery tested concept models, decision models and rule statements, and returned the important negative finding that not all legislation is suitable for machine consumption.458 These are comparative foundations, not sources of Pakistani authority.

20.2.4 Two implications of that framing are usually missed. The first is institutional: if an official machine-consumable version exists, some body must own it, and ownership of the coded version is a species of authority over the rule. A drafting office that publishes a model claims meaning; a regulator claims it within its competence; a vendor claims it with neither, and accuracy does not cure that — an accurate vendor model is simply the more persuasive one. The second is legislative. Coding a rule at the drafting stage exposes ambiguity early, but it also creates pressure to draft rules that code well. Determinate, element-based rules are easier to represent than standards, purposive tests and multi-factor balancing, so a programme that quietly prefers the representable narrows the legislature’s choice of legal technique without proposing that narrowing as policy. The Better Rules finding that not all legislation is suitable for machine consumption is therefore not only a technical limit but a constitutional caution: a provision may resist machine consumption because the legislature conferred judgment rather than specified an outcome. Which it is, in any given case, is for the drafter and the court — not for a modelling programme to answer for itself.

20.2.5 In Pakistan the question has a partial statutory answer. The Virtual Assets Act allocates classification, licensing and supervisory functions to PVARA and reserves prescribed detail to Rules and Regulations; the Digital Nation Pakistan Act gives the Pakistan Digital Authority standards, reference-architecture and coordination functions, preserving data custodians’ control and requiring avoidance of overlap with other mandates. No provision authorising any body to publish a machine-consumable version of the law with legal effect was located in the provisions read for this chapter, neither Act having been read in full. That is recorded as a `[GAP]` — not located, rather than confirmed absent — and it is not to be filled by inference from a technical standard, a reference architecture or a vendor’s implementation.

20.2.6 The distinction between machine-readable, machine-consumable and machine-executable should be maintained. A provision with a stable identifier, dates and subject tags is machine-readable; a structured obligation a service can query is machine-consumable; a rule that evaluates inputs and returns a result is executable. Each transition adds interpretation, and so adds a point at which error, institutional bias or silent legal change can enter.

20.2.7 The terms describe capability, not authority. Standardised identifiers and metadata can improve access without purporting to decide cases: the European Legislation Identifier uses persistent identifiers and structured metadata so that legislation can be accessed, exchanged and reused across systems.459 Pakistan can learn from that publication architecture without importing European law or assuming that linked data resolves statutory interpretation.

20.2.8 Three propositions follow. First, official status is a legal question: a government-hosted file may be a consultation draft, guidance, a convenience copy or an operative instrument, and a machine must carry that status rather than infer authority from a domain name. Secondly, equivalence between text and model cannot be self-declared by the developer; it requires legal mapping, test cases and institutional approval. Thirdly, even an officially published computational model would require an express rule about its legal effect; until Parliament or valid delegated legislation says otherwise, the authenticated text and the competent decision remain controlling.

20.2.9 This treatise therefore uses a bounded formulation: Qānūn-Map may make legal requirements more legible, traceable and testable; it does not make public power self-executing. “Code is law” is rejected descriptively and constitutionally. Code can constrain a workflow, but only law supplies the State’s authority to burden a person, and only an authorised process turns proved facts into an adverse public decision.

20.3 Qānūn-Map: a human-governed legal knowledge architecture

20.3.1 Qānūn-Map is the proposed name for a linked legal knowledge and decision-support architecture, developed within the Jurisprudence of Intelligent Order. It is not a new legal order and, at the present stage, is not a deployed public system. Its purpose is to preserve the path from source to implementation in a form usable by lawyers, drafters, regulators, service designers, engineers, regulated persons and reviewers.

20.3.2 The name is chosen deliberately. Qānūn is law; a map is a representation of terrain that is useful precisely because it is not the terrain. A map claiming to be the ground would be worse than no map, since it would suppress the inquiry — is this representation accurate, current and complete? — that makes representation safe. Qānūn-Map is therefore designed to be interrogable at every point about its own fidelity. It is not a case-management system, though it must connect to one; not a legal-research product, though it depends on the same source discipline; not an expert system replacing legal advice; and not a compliance-certification service. Each is a different object with a different failure mode, and conflating them is the shortest route to a system that appears authoritative because it is comprehensive.

20.3.3 The architecture contains seven connected stores or services:

1. an authoritative-source register containing instruments, issuers, official locations, authentication evidence, dates, status and checksums;

2. a norm map that divides instruments into addressable provisions and records definitions, powers, duties, exceptions, amendments, dependencies and conflicts;

3. an obligation model expressing the actor, activity, condition, duty, exception, evidence, institution, decision, reason and remedy;

4. an evidence schema defining what a supplied fact means, its source, custodian, quality, time and permissible use;

5. a test suite containing ordinary cases, boundary cases, missing-input cases, conflicts, amendments and prohibited outcomes;

6. a decision-file service that records the model and source version used, questions asked, inputs supplied, path, warnings, human officer, reasons and action; and

7. a review and change layer for correction, appeal, legal update, regression testing, rollback, publication and audit.

20.3.4 A recurring architectural error is to begin with a single consolidated database of everything and to derive rules from it afterwards. That inverts the dependency. Authority is not a property that can be recovered from aggregated content; it must be carried from the source and preserved through every transformation. A store that mixes an operative section, a consultation draft, an explanatory circular and an internal note as undifferentiated “legal content” has already destroyed the distinction the system exists to protect.

Figure 20.1 — From legal text to a reviewable Qānūn-Map

Figure 20.1 — reading note. The figure traces the end-to-end pipeline from an authenticated Gazette instrument, through the provision and metadata register and the lawyer-drafter norm map, to the structured obligation and evidence model, the executable tests and routing, the human decision file, and the reasons, notice and remedy that follow from it. The review, correction and appeal loop returns to the norm map rather than to the output, so that a defect is repaired where it originated rather than patched where it surfaced. A draft, gap or uncertain source connects to the model by a blocking relationship only: it prevents operative use rather than feeding it. Security, privacy and audit controls attach to the register, the test layer and the decision file. Labels, sequence and line meaning — not colour alone — carry the figure’s analysis.

```mermaid

flowchart TD

A["Authenticated Gazette instrument"] --> B["Provision and metadata register"]

B --> C["Lawyer-drafter norm map"]

C --> D["Structured obligation and evidence model"]

D --> E["Executable tests and routing"]

E --> F["Human decision file"]

F --> G["Reasons, notice and remedy"]

G --> H["Review, correction and appeal"]

H --> C

I["Draft, gap or uncertain source"] -. "blocks operative use" .-> D

J["Security, privacy and audit controls"] --- B

J --- E

J --- F

```

Source note: Author’s architecture derived from the Pakistani hierarchy and Chapters 13–19, informed comparatively by OECD Rules as Code, New Zealand Better Rules and the European Legislation Identifier. The arrows show provenance and governance, not a transfer of legal authority to code.

20.3.5 The architecture must allow movement in both directions. An amendment flows from source registration through remapping and testing before release. An appeal or incident flows backwards: the reviewer reconstructs the source, model, inputs and human act, identifies whether the defect was legal, factual, technical or procedural, and corrects the appropriate layer. A system storing only the final output cannot support that inquiry.

20.3.6 Qānūn-Map also separates a legal model from an administrative business rule. A statute may require an application “in such form and manner” as prescribed. A regulator may validly prescribe fields. An office may then adopt internal routing, file-naming and workload practices. Those layers have different authority. Internal convenience must not become an undisclosed condition of eligibility, and a technical validation must not reject an application because a non-statutory preference was coded as mandatory.

20.3.7 Every rule object should be readable by a lawyer without executing software, displaying at minimum its plain-language proposition, exact source locator, status, effective period, institution, input definition, output meaning, escalation condition, test results and change history. Open publication is preferred for general legal models and test cases, subject to security, privacy, investigative secrecy and intellectual-property constraints lawfully identified. The public should be able to see why the model asks a question and what it will not decide.

20.3.8 Two labels are essential. `[DRAFT]` means text or logic exists but is not operative authority. It may be used in a sandbox or policy simulation only if every screen and output preserves that status and segregates it from live decisions. `[GAP]` means a required source, rule, fact, institutional assignment or remedy has not been verified. A gap is not permission for the developer to select the most convenient answer. In an operative pathway, either label must stop the affected conclusion and route the matter to an authorised human process.

20.4 Normative hierarchy, source status and version control

20.4.1 Qānūn-Map should encode authority before it encodes outcomes. That authority cannot be represented as one universal ladder in which every source simply ranks above or below every other. It must preserve six distinct legal dimensions.

Table 20.3 — Six authority dimensions and the rule each imposes on the model

Authority dimensionRule for the model
constitutional supremacyno statute, delegated instrument or administrative act may be treated as valid authority contrary to the Constitution as lawfully interpreted
legislative competenceidentify whether the matter and instrument are federal or provincial and apply the constitutional distribution and conflict rules; do not assume that one legislature’s Act universally ranks above the other’s
delegated legislationlink each Rule, Regulation, notification or other instrument to its enabling Act, maker, procedure, Gazette status, scope and consistency limits; instrument names alone do not establish an inter se rank
judicial authorityrecord court, bench, date, precedential status, issue and material factual setting; precedent operates through the judicial hierarchy and legal doctrine, not as another paragraph in a legislative stack
administrative actidentify the statutory power, delegate, case, reasons and review status; an administrative decision may determine a case within power but is not equivalent to general legislation
guidance and operationslabel standards, circulars, forms, FAQs and internal instructions by their actual legal effect; publication in software does not promote them into binding law

20.4.2 The Virtual Assets Act illustrates why this matters. The Act came into force at once and authorises federal Rules by Gazette notification and PVARA Regulations through the statutory procedure. Its direct provisions coexist with matters left to prescription. The official material checked for this treatise continued to distinguish the Act, NOC stage, draft VASP Regulations and prospective full licensing.460 A model may use an operative statutory proposition where its elements are sufficiently clear. It must not fill a prescribed-detail gap from a consultation draft and then label the result current law.

20.4.3 Every source object should contain at least the following fields.

Table 20.4 — Minimum content of a source object

FieldRequired content
identityjurisdiction, instrument type, official title, number and stable provision ID
authorityissuing body, enabling provision and authentication evidence
status`OPERATIVE_VERIFIED`, `[DRAFT]`, `[GAP]`, `HISTORICAL`, `SUPERSEDED`, `SUSPENDED` or `NOT_READ`
timemaking, publication, commencement, effective-from, effective-to and transition dates
textexact provision, language, official locator and any authorised correction
relationshipamends, repeals, saves, overrides, depends on, conflicts with or implements
integrityfile checksum, extraction method, reviewer and last verified date
model linkrule objects, test suite, implementation version and release approval

20.4.4 The system should distinguish source version, model version, engine version and service version. A statute can remain unchanged while a faulty model is corrected. A model can remain unchanged while the evaluation engine changes. A service interface can change without altering either. Combining all four under “latest version” makes audit impossible.

20.4.5 A worked example shows why the source stream in particular cannot be collapsed. Suppose an applicant’s conduct occurred while only the Act and the NOC stage were operative, and the question — was that conduct within the perimeter when it was carried on? — is asked after Regulations have been notified. The answer depends on the text that governed the conduct, not on the text most recent in the store. The question must be stated before the version can be chosen: a different question, such as what the applicant must now do to be licensed, is governed by the current text. A system that resolves both from a single consolidated “current law” view will answer the first confidently and wrongly, and will do so identically on every run; reproducibility does not mitigate that error but industrialises it. The decision file must therefore record the question asked, the version applied and the legal reason for applying it — commencement, transition, saving or express retrospective effect — as first-class fields, not as free text in a note. The other three streams need the same discipline for a different reason: each can change while the source stands still, so an irreproducible result may reflect a corrected model or a replaced engine rather than any change in the law.

20.4.6 Updates must never be silent. A source change enters quarantine; a legal owner verifies authority and temporal effect; the model is amended in a separate branch; the full test suite runs; affected institutions approve within their functions; and a signed release states which cases may change. If urgent legal change precedes a tested model, the safe response is to suspend the affected automated route and use a human process under the new law. Continuing to run a known superseded model for convenience is not digital continuity; it is systematic legal error.

20.4.7 Quarantine is a legal control, not a technical convenience. When a source changes, the affected branches must stop producing operative outputs before anyone assesses whether the change is material, : a wrong answer given under a superseded model must afterwards be found, revisited and unwound, whereas a suspension is visible when it occurs and can be carried by the human route. Suspension must not be silent either — the interruption falls on the person waiting, and §20.8‘s rule holds that an outage cannot extinguish a statutory time limit or a right to make representations. Release requires a named legal owner’s verification of authority and temporal effect, not an engineer’s judgment that the difference looks small.

20.4.8 Temporal logic deserves separate testing. Publication, commencement, transition, savings, repeal and retrospective effect are not interchangeable dates. Where a court has interpreted a provision, the model should link the decision and its precedential status without converting a fact-sensitive holding into a universal Boolean rule.

20.5 A machine-readable obligation model

20.5.1 The smallest useful Qānūn-Map object is not a paragraph of code. It is a legal proposition whose elements and consequences can be inspected independently. For a VASP-perimeter screen, the object may be expressed across twelve elements.

Table 20.5 — Twelve elements of a VASP-perimeter obligation object

ElementStructured representationHuman/legal boundary
actoridentified person; legal form; role; verified entity and representative identifierswhether multiple actors form one service or exercise control
activitydescribed function, customer journey, asset flow, custody, interface, remuneration and jurisdictionclassification by substance, function, use and economic effect
territorial conditioncarried on, or held out as carried on, in or from Pakistantargeting, representations and cross-border facts may be disputed
business conditionbusiness and professional basisisolated activity, group allocation and commercial substance require evidence
relational conditionservice to third partiesprincipal/agent, own-account and customer relationships require legal analysis
service categorysection 18 and Schedule I candidate categoryambiguous or combined services require reasoned classification
exception/perimetersection 2 exclusions and SBP/SECP or other connected lawno automatic exemption; competent regulator coordination may be required
current legal propositionthe Act’s scope, VASP definition, service categories and NOC/licensing provisions apply according to their termsexact NOC, licence, unauthorised-activity or transition consequence depends on operative law and proved facts
recommended administrative routingroute a potentially in-scope case to PVARA without representing that the screen proves a licence, exemption or breachthis is a safe workflow recommendation, not a new statutory duty triggered merely by screening uncertainty
evidenceterms, user flow, entity records, wallet/key control, fees, transaction samples and marketingauthenticity, completeness, privilege and weight remain reviewable
institutionPVARA for VAA classification; connected institution for its own statutory perimetercoordination does not transfer statutory competence
reason/remedycited path, missing facts, decision-maker, review and appeal routeonly the competent body can make the relevant order or adjudication

20.5.2 The Virtual Assets Act supplies the principal source chain. Section 2 states the Pakistan nexus and express exclusions. Section 3 defines a VASP as a person who, as a business, provides one or more virtual-asset services to third parties on a professional basis. Section 9(1)(f) authorises PVARA to classify by substance and economic effect, with consultation where SBP or SECP characteristics appear. Section 18 and Schedule I identify service categories. Section 19 then begins the NOC and licence application sequence and requires written reasons for refusal at the NOC stage.461

20.5.3 These provisions contain both formal and evaluative elements. Code can check that a declared entity identifier exists, that a date is well formed, that required evidence fields are present, or that supplied values follow a declared branch. It cannot establish from an applicant’s checkbox that an operation is “professional”, that an arrangement is truly own-account, or that no securities, payments, foreign-exchange or deposit-taking perimeter is engaged.

20.5.4 The distinction needs to be drawn more finely than in two classes, and it does not run across all twelve elements. Four — the current legal proposition, the recommended administrative routing, the institution and the reason or remedy — are not inputs at all; they are the object’s outputs and its allocation of competence, settled by the law rather than by the case. The remaining eight are inputs, and they divide into three classes. Some are formal: a registration number either exists in the companies register or does not; a date is either well-formed or not; a declared service category either carries a source link or does not. Some are evidential: whether the supplied terms of service, fee schedule and wallet-control material establish the asserted facts is a question of proof, and the system can record what was supplied and by whom without determining weight. Some are evaluative: whether an activity is carried on as a business and on a professional basis, whether an arrangement is genuinely own-account, whether a combined offering falls within a listed category by substance and economic effect. Section 9(1)(f)’s classification function is evaluative on any reading, and the consultation requirement attaching where SBP or SECP characteristics appear allocates the question to named institutions. The statute does not address computability and nothing should be read into it on that subject; but a function the legislature has routed through named regulators is not one a model may perform in their place. A model that renders an evaluative element as a checkbox has not simplified the law; it has silently transferred a statutory judgment to whoever ticks the box.

20.5.5 An automation model should therefore classify functions by permitted use, not by optimism about technical capability:

  • publication and retrieval: source discovery, provision linking and status display;
  • syntactic validation: format, completeness, arithmetic, date and identifier checks;
  • screening and routing: candidate classification and identification of the competent human pathway;
  • decision support: comparison of evidence with declared criteria, with an authorised officer independently responsible for reasons and result; and
  • prohibited automatic consequence: refusal, licence grant or variation, sanction, freeze, tax assessment, liability finding, merits determination or appeal disposition without the human authority and process required by law.

20.5.6 Some calculations are highly determinate yet still depend on human-controlled inputs. A deadline calculation requires the correct triggering event, communication date, governing version and any lawful extension; it can be reproducible while the legal premise is contested. The output must therefore show the answer and the assumptions on which it rests.

20.5.7 Reproducibility and correctness are independent properties, and confusing them is a recurring error in demonstration projects. A model that returns the same output for the same inputs has established determinism. It has established nothing about whether the inputs were true, whether the mapped provision was the governing one, whether the mapping preserved that provision’s exceptions, or whether the institution running it had power to act on the result. Determinism is a precondition of audit, not evidence of legality.

20.5.8 Missing information should produce a typed state, not a guessed value. `UNKNOWN` means a fact was not supplied or verified; `[GAP]` that the governing source or institutional mechanism is absent or unresolved; `[DRAFT]` that the candidate rule lacks operative status; `CONFLICT` that two apparently applicable authorities or data sources cannot be reconciled. Each state should generate the responsible owner and next lawful action. None should default to refusal — and none should default to approval, which is the failure mode of a system tested only on clear approvals, just as over-routing is the failure mode of one tested only on enforcement cases. The lawful default for an unresolved element is neither outcome, but a routed question with a named owner and a stated next step.

20.6 Demonstration: the VASP activity-perimeter screen

20.6.1 The project contains a VASP activity-perimeter demonstrator. This chapter does not present it as a regulator product or licence-readiness tool. It is a research artefact with a JSON rule map, three input cases, a runner and saved results. Its declared version is `0.1.0-demo` and its declared status `research_demo`; its notice states that the Gazette remains authoritative, that PVARA and other competent regulators retain authority, and that no licence or legal conclusion is produced automatically.462 The last phrase is imprecise, because the outputs do express tentative screening conclusions. The accurate boundary is that the demonstrator produces no final, binding or statutory determination.

20.6.2 The map asks six questions in sequence: Pakistan nexus; professional business basis; service to third parties; apparent Schedule I match; absence of an identified express exclusion; and absence of an unresolved connected-regulator issue. Its metadata marks every node as requiring human control but does not define the required role; a controlled redesign should distinguish user assertions, clerical authentication, legally qualified classification, connected-regulator concurrence, override authority and the final statutory decision. The terminal branches either say that a proposition has not been established on the supplied facts or route the matter for human classification.

20.6.3 On 16 August 2026 the saved runner was executed against the three saved cases. The results carried the same SHA-256 checksum before and after execution. That establishes reproducibility of this run in the checked environment; it validates neither the legal model, the underlying facts nor the deployment architecture.

Table 20.6 — Reproduced demonstrator cases and the residual human questions

Test caseSupplied issueReproduced path outcomeWhat remains human
D1 — custodial walletall six supplied predicates marked true`ESCALATE_HUMAN`; potential VASP route to PVARAsource authentication, factual proof, classification, NOC/licensing stage and connected permissions
D2 — ambiguous software providerSchedule I match marked false`ESCALATE_HUMAN`; service classification requiredwhether software, interface, custody, execution, control or remuneration constitutes a listed service
D3 — fiat-referenced payment tokenconnected-perimeter conflict marked unresolved`ESCALATE_HUMAN`; interagency classification requiredPVARA, SBP, SECP or other competence, payment/FX treatment and applicable entry route

20.6.4 All three saved cases returned `ESCALATE_HUMAN`. At the research stage that is the desired result, but it is not evidence that the boundary was drawn in the right place: three cases that all escalate have no discriminating power, being equally consistent with a boundary correctly drawn, one drawn far too conservatively, and a model that escalates unconditionally whatever it is given. There is no negative control, so nothing about the design is tested by it. What can be said is narrower — the terminal branches do not assert a determination, the most positive saying only “potential VASP route to PVARA” — and whether a user would treat it as one is a separate question on which §20.8‘s automation-bias analysis counsels against assumption.

20.6.5 Such a model also has, by construction, no measured administrative value; the honest inference is not that the boundary is wrong but that the value case has not been made. Escalation may later be reduced by removing questions the law does not ask, or by resolving formal elements that never required judgment; through an evidential element only where the evidence is obtained and its sufficiency recorded, never by treating an unproved fact as established; and never by converting an evaluative element into a default. Hence the link to the capacity-and-value gate in §20.10: the test of a safe model and the test of a useful one are different, and passing the first does not create a case for deployment.

20.6.6 The most instructive defect is the representation of exclusion and connected-perimeter questions as Boolean inputs. Each is a legal conclusion, not a fact: whether a token falls within an express exclusion, and whether a securities, payments, foreign-exchange or deposit-taking perimeter is engaged, are determinations requiring an identified officer, stated evidence, reasons and a validity period. Presenting them as inputs makes the output conditional on conclusions the model did not reach and cannot display. A corrected design replaces each with a human determination object carrying the determining institution, the officer, the date, the evidence relied on and an expiry, so that a stale determination fails visibly rather than silently.

20.6.7 What the demonstration establishes is determinism and nothing more, on the distinction drawn at §20.5; it is silent on whether the model contains every relevant provision, whether the cited extract is the latest authoritative text, whether the engine is secure, and whether a regulator has approved its labels, automation classes or outcomes.

20.6.8 Three cases are also too few to constitute a legal-control asset; the classes the saved set omits, and the control each would exercise, are identified at §20.9.

20.6.9 The label “licence readiness” must also be used carefully. The existing map is an activity-perimeter screen: it does not test incorporation, NOC documentation, controllers, key individuals, fit-and-proper criteria, capital, customer assets, AML/CFT, technology, governance, outsourcing, business continuity, complaints or wind-down. A readiness module would need a separate, status-controlled obligation set derived from operative requirements. Where required detail is `[DRAFT]` or `[GAP]`, the system may prepare an evidence inventory or simulate proposed requirements, but it cannot present readiness as legal compliance.

Figure 20.2 — Mandatory human escalation flow

Figure 20.2 — reading note. The flow begins where a user or officer supplies evidence and passes it through source, status and version checks. The first decision point asks whether the governing material is operative and complete; a `[DRAFT]`, `[GAP]`, conflict or stale source sends the branch to quarantine, where no operative outcome may be produced until the legal or source owner authenticates, amends or identifies the missing authority — and the flow then returns to the same check rather than proceeding. Only an operative and complete source reaches deterministic validation or screening. The second decision point asks whether a missing or contested fact, an interpretation, a discretion, a connected perimeter or an adverse outcome is engaged; if so the matter goes to a competent officer who reviews the evidence and records reasons. If not, the model generates an assistive result and a full trace, and that branch too passes through a human checkpoint — a person confirms the permitted administrative use — before either route converges on notice, correction, review or appeal, and from there on audit, learning and model correction. Two limits of the figure should be read with it. The quarantine loop as drawn returns to the same completeness check and has no exit edge, so where the source owner can only identify a missing authority rather than supply it, the drawn flow does not terminate; the exit is the one stated in prose at §20.4 — suspend the affected automated route and carry the matter through the human process — and it must be read into the figure. Nor does the figure state a time limit for a quarantined matter, and §20.8’s rule governs: a stall in the system cannot extinguish a statutory time limit or a right to make representations. Labels, sequence and line meaning — not colour alone — carry the figure’s analysis.

```mermaid

flowchart TD

A["User or officer supplies evidence"] --> B["Source, status and version checks"]

B --> C{"Operative and complete?"}

C -- "No: DRAFT, GAP, conflict or stale source" --> Q["Quarantine model branch; no operative outcome"]

Q --> R["Legal/source owner authenticates, amends or identifies missing authority"]

R --> C

C -- "Yes" --> D["Deterministic validation or screening"]

D --> E{"Missing or contested fact, interpretation, discretion, connected perimeter or adverse outcome?"}

E -- "Yes" --> H["Escalate to competent officer"]

E -- "No" --> F["Generate assistive result and full trace"]

H --> I["Competent officer reviews evidence and records reasons"]

I --> J["Notice, correction, review or appeal route"]

F --> K["Human confirms permitted administrative use"]

K --> J

J --> L["Audit, learning and model correction"]

```

20.6.10 The correct public interface should make these limits visible before a user relies on the result.

20.7 Regulatory data, interoperability, privacy and evidence

20.7.1 A rule model is only as reliable as its source and input data. Interoperability should therefore begin with identifiers and meaning, not bulk data transfer. The system needs stable identifiers for instruments, provisions, organisations, licences, permissions, officers, applications, evidence items, decisions, cases and model releases. Each shared field requires a definition, lawful purpose, source custodian, validation rule, time quality and correction route.

20.7.2 The Digital Nation Pakistan Act defines digital public infrastructure to include identity, data exchange, cloud and open-data components and gives the Pakistan Digital Authority important standards and coordination functions. It also preserves control and responsibility of designated data custodians and expressly requires avoidance of overlap with other regulatory mandates.463 That supports a common technical layer; it does not create permission for PVARA, PDA or a vendor to collect or combine any dataset that would be useful.

20.7.3 The data architecture should use minimum disclosure. An eligibility or perimeter query often requires verification of a proposition rather than disclosure of the underlying record. A system may need to know that a company exists and that a representative holds a valid role, not retrieve every filing or personal identifier. Access should be role-based and purpose-limited; sensitive evidence should be encrypted, logged and segregated; test data should be synthetic or lawfully de-identified; and public rule models should not expose investigative thresholds whose disclosure would defeat a lawful function.

20.7.4 Chapter 13 established that data protection, cybersecurity and evidence are separate legal questions. A secure database can still be unlawful; a lawful collection can still be insecure; and an accurate system log can still require proof of attribution and integrity. Qānūn-Map should preserve the source of an input, who supplied or changed it, when it was valid, the method of verification and any contest. Hashes and digital signatures can assist integrity and authentication, but they cannot prove that the original factual assertion was true.464

20.7.5 Authentication at the publication end deserves the same discipline. A source register can record a checksum for the file it retrieved, but a checksum computed by the consumer proves only that the file has not changed since download; it does not establish that the file is the instrument the issuing authority made. Closing that distance requires action by the publisher, not the reader: instruments signed by the authority that issued them, published with their own integrity value, and retrievable in a stable, machine-addressable form. No such mechanism was located for the instruments on which this chapter depends. That is recorded as a `[GAP]` — not located in the checked material, rather than confirmed to be absent — and until it is closed, every model relying on a downloaded instrument carries an authentication risk that no amount of internal hashing can remove. Two artefacts here should be read subject to that limitation: the `integrity` field at Table 20.4 and the `legal source` row of Figure 20.3 both record a checksum, and neither can mean more than consumer-side integrity until publication-side authentication exists. Figure 20.1‘s entry node states the condition the architecture requires, not one presently shown to be satisfied.

20.7.6 Evidence exports must be intelligible without the live system. A decision file should contain the operative source text or stable official locator, all relevant versions, inputs, provenance, branch path, reasons, human approvals, notices and later changes in a durable format. Retention must follow legal purpose and proceedings, not the convenience of indefinite storage. A person should be able to correct an erroneous factual record without rewriting the historical fact that the earlier decision used it.

20.7.7 Interoperability also requires graceful failure. If an identity, company, tax, sanctions or regulator interface is unavailable, the service should show the failure and offer a lawful alternative. “No response from another database” must not be translated into “not eligible” or “non-compliant”. Cross-agency APIs should carry status and timestamp, not just values, and each institution must remain responsible for the field it authoritatively maintains.

20.8 Human authority, explanation and contestability

20.8.1 Human control is not satisfied by placing an officer after an automated result if the officer lacks time, evidence, training or authority to depart from it. Meaningful human judgment requires the power to ask for more information, change a classification, refuse the model’s recommendation, record reasons and trigger correction of a defective rule. The reviewer must know which parts were calculated and which were legal or factual assumptions.

20.8.2 The workflow must also guard against automation bias. A prominently displayed score or “recommended outcome” may become functionally decisive even when a form permits override. Assurance should therefore examine actual override rates, time available for review, whether officers receive the underlying evidence rather than only the output, and whether departures attract inappropriate managerial pressure. For contested or adverse cases, the interface should present the legal question and evidence before any system recommendation, so that the officer forms an independent view.

20.8.3 The Constitution requires public power to be exercised through law, fair process and legally responsible institutions. The VAA allocates classification and licensing functions to PVARA, requires written reasons for refusal at the NOC stage and provides an appellate structure for persons aggrieved by Authority orders.465 Software cannot become the statutory Authority, an appellate tribunal or the Supreme Court. Nor can a generic “human in the loop” transfer one regulator’s power to another institution.

20.8.4 Every result that may affect a person should disclose:

1. the purpose and non-binding or binding status of the process;

2. the source instruments and exact versions used;

3. the material facts supplied, retrieved or inferred;

4. the rule path and calculations;

5. missing information, conflicts, `[DRAFT]` and `[GAP]` states;

6. the responsible institution and named or identifiable decision function;

7. the human reasons for any operative decision;

8. how to correct facts, make representations and obtain the record; and

9. the complaint, review, appeal or court route available under law.

20.8.5 Explanation should track the actual decision. A generic statement that “requirements were not met” is not cured by attaching hundreds of rules. The officer should identify the decisive legal provision, factual finding, evidence accepted or rejected, treatment of a material representation and consequence selected. Where security or investigation law justifies withholding particular information, the limitation itself needs authority and review; secrecy should not become the default explanation for system opacity.

20.8.6 No automated tool should make or execute an adverse legal decision merely because its prediction is accurate on historical data. Prediction and authority are different. Historical outcomes may encode inconsistent administration, exclusion or error. A machine-learning score may help prioritise a review only under an approved purpose and assurance regime; it should not supply an undisclosed substantive criterion. For the bounded programme proposed here, the preferable core is transparent deterministic logic, with analytics kept separate and never allowed to overwrite the legal rule path.

20.8.7 Contestability also improves the model. Successful challenges, withdrawn decisions and unusual cases should enter the regression suite after legal review. That does not mean that a single officer’s decision rewrites the law. It means the programme tests whether the model omitted an exception, misrepresented an ambiguity, relied on poor data or invited users to answer a legal conclusion as if it were a simple fact.

20.8.8 A remedy must remain usable outside the platform. Loss of an account, service outage or inaccessible interface cannot extinguish a statutory time limit or right to make representations. Notices should identify an alternative channel, and the complete record should be obtainable in a durable human-readable form. The reviewing institution should be able to suspend reliance on a disputed model without disabling the underlying legal process.

20.9 Governance, assurance and controlled change

20.9.1 Qānūn-Map requires institutional governance before scale. The minimum operating model separates five roles: authoritative-source custodian; legal-model owner; responsible regulatory decision owner; engineering and security owner; and an assurance function able to stop release. No one person or vendor should authenticate the law, interpret it, write the implementation, approve it and certify the result.

20.9.2 Each model release should pass six gates.

Table 20.7 — Release gates and the proof each requires

GateRequired proof
sourceauthenticated instrument, status, dates, hierarchy and amendment check
legal mappingprovision-by-provision derivation, unresolved interpretations and competent owner
datadefinitions, lawful access, provenance, correction, quality and privacy assessment
technicalreviewed code, pinned dependencies, security tests, reproducible build and rollback
casesordinary, boundary, missing, conflict, draft, gap, adversarial and prohibited-outcome tests
administrativeauthorised use, trained officer, reasons template, notice, record and working remedy

20.9.3 The inspected demonstrator supplies five concrete pre-pilot defects for those gates. Its engine is imported from another research workspace and must be pinned, reviewed and hashed within an approved build. Its exclusion and connected-perimeter inputs are Boolean values although they are legal conclusions, as §20.6 explains. Its exclusion predicate cites sections 3 and 5 although the principal express exclusions appear in section 2(2), so the map must be corrected and regression-tested. Its generic `hcc_required` flag does not allocate user, clerical, legal, inter-regulator, override and final-decision roles. Its notice overstates the boundary, as §20.6 records.

20.9.4 The test suite is a legal-control asset. It should include cases whose correct output is “unknown”, “wrong institution”, “draft only”, “source conflict”, “human classification”, “insufficient authority” or “do not proceed”. The default-direction risks are those identified at §20.5.

20.9.5 Measured against that standard the saved demonstrator set is deficient in five classes, each testing a control it does not exercise: a missing-input case, so that an unverified element yields `UNKNOWN` with a routed owner; a `[DRAFT]` case and a `[GAP]` case, so that a proposed rule and an unverified authority block the branch rather than supply it; a source-change case, so that an amendment quarantines the branch while the pre-change version stays retrievable; a conflict case, so that two irreconcilable authorities yield `CONFLICT` and a route to the competent institutions; and a prohibited-outcome case, so that no combination of inputs can drive a refusal, grant, sanction or other adverse consequence. That last exercises the boundary on which the design rests; its absence is the gravest omission. A negative control, a case that should complete without escalating, is required alongside them; without one, escalation behaviour cannot be distinguished from unconditional escalation.

20.9.6 Change control requires dual approval by legal and technical owners. A source update triggers an impact report identifying affected rules, tests, services and prior cases. Material changes require notice and, where rights or duties change, the legal process for the underlying instrument—not only a software release. Rollback must restore the last approved model and preserve decisions already taken for review, and the audit log must include rejected releases and emergency overrides.

20.9.7 Procurement cannot outsource responsibility. A contract should require open data and rule formats where lawful, documentation, source and dependency disclosure, portability, security obligations, incident notice, audit access, exit assistance and continued access to decision records. Proprietary code must not prevent PVARA, a tribunal or a court from understanding the basis of a public decision; vendor performance claims are not evidence of lawful deployment.

20.9.8 Governance must address conflicts and participation. Regulated firms may properly test whether a rule model reflects operational reality, but should not control its interpretation, acceptance tests or release for requirements that bind them. Applicants, customers, lawyers, accessibility specialists and frontline officers should be able to expose burdens and edge cases through a recorded process. Consultation evidence should be published or summarised with reasons, confidential material remaining protected under identified authority.

20.9.9 Independent assurance should sample source pinpoints, reproduce results, challenge edge cases, inspect access and change logs, test the remedy, and ask whether the system has become functionally mandatory though described as optional. Material incidents include not only cyber compromise but use of a draft as operative law, a stale model, inability to explain a result, systematic override by staff, inaccessible review and any automatic adverse consequence outside authority.

20.9.10 Programme metrics should measure legal and administrative quality: source defects found, unresolved gaps, disagreement categories, corrected inputs, time and cost to complete the lawful process, successful challenges, security events and remedy availability. A high number of automated completions is not success if people cannot understand or contest them. Assurance should report residual defects and hold a defined suspension threshold.

20.10 National Digital Masterplan integration and institutional ownership

20.10.1 The Digital Nation Pakistan Act provides the planning and coordination setting for a future programme. The National Digital Commission approves the Masterplan and provides strategic direction. The Pakistan Digital Authority develops, implements, monitors and periodically updates it; coordinates across governments and regulators; develops technology standards and reference architectures; and monitors alignment. The Act requires sectoral and implementation plans, consultation, milestones and annual review.466

20.10.2 That framework can supply the horizontal layer: source and metadata standards, reference architecture, identity and data-exchange conventions, accessibility, cloud and security baselines, procurement patterns and programme monitoring. It does not make PDA the VAA decision-maker. Section 8(g) itself requires avoidance of overlap and conflict with other regulatory mandates. PVARA remains the vertical legal owner of VAA perimeter, licensing and supervision; SBP, SECP, FMU, FBR and other institutions remain owners of their respective law.

20.10.3 The institutional design should be recorded in the relevant sectoral and implementation plan, with budget, staff, milestones, risks, assurance and public outcome measures. A technical reference architecture without these owners would repeat the implementation gap the Masterplan is intended to address.

Table 20.8 — Proposed accountable owners and their boundaries

FunctionProposed accountable ownerBoundary
cross-government legal-data and service standardPDA under an approved Masterplan/valid instrumenttechnical coordination; no sector decision transfer
VAA source and obligation modelPVARA legal owner with Gazette/source custodian supportonly operative VAA material may drive live use
connected financial perimetereach competent regulator, through a recorded coordination processconcurrence or referral does not erase statutory competence
model engineering and operationapproved public team or procured supplier under institutional controlsupplier does not own legal interpretation or public decision
assurancefunctionally independent legal, technical, security and administrative reviewersauthority to stop or suspend release
public reportingPDA for programme indicators; each regulator for decisions and outcomes within its lawaggregated reporting must preserve privacy and legal status

20.10.4 Before an institutional shadow pilot and again before scale, a capacity-and-value gate should test whether the service improves rather than duplicates administration. The baseline should record current processing time, error and rework categories, officer time, unresolved referrals, applicant burden and cost. The pilot should identify which clerical or deterministic tasks it can actually complete, the expected percentage and volume of human escalations, required legal and technical staffing, source-maintenance cost, service levels and operating cost per case. If nearly every case receives another full review, the system adds delay without reducing legal risk. The programme should then narrow the use case, redesign it or stop. Progress requires an adopted benefit threshold and a termination rule, not an assumption that more digitisation equals more capacity.

20.10.5 At the evidence cut-off, the official National Digital Masterplan material reviewed for this treatise evidenced consultation and roadmap development, not an approved digital-assets Rules-as-Code sector plan.467 The proposed programme must therefore be described as a recommendation for possible inclusion through the Act’s approval and consultation process. Neither this treatise nor its demonstrator is the Masterplan.

20.10.6 Section 28 of the Digital Nation Pakistan Act also requires care. Its override provision preserves stronger data-rights and cybersecurity measures, and persistent conflicts are to be addressed through consultation, Commission action within law or proposed legislative amendment. It is not a machine rule allowing a shared platform to select the “higher” institutional mandate or transfer PVARA, SBP, SECP, FBR or judicial powers to PDA.468

20.11 A phased demonstration programme—and the limit of execution

20.11.1 The programme should advance by evidence gates, not by announcing a national platform and filling it later.

20.11.2 Phase 0 — source integrity. Establish authenticated source registers for the VAA, valid subordinate instruments and directly connected law. Assign provision identifiers, status, commencement, amendment and official-location metadata. Publicly separate operative, draft, historical and missing material. No executable case outcome is required.

20.11.3 Phase 1 — controlled research prototype. Refactor the existing perimeter screen into a self-contained, reproducible package. Replace legal-conclusion checkboxes with human determination objects. Add missing-input, draft, gap, cross-regulator and source-change cases. Publish the rule map, limitations and test results as research. Success is faithful traceability and safe escalation, not approval accuracy.

20.11.4 Phase 2 — institutional shadow pilot. With PVARA and connected institutions’ approval, trained officers run the model alongside—not inside—the live process. It cannot affect an applicant. Compare its questions and routing with human files; record disagreement; test privacy, security, accessibility and record export; and verify that the real review route works.

20.11.5 Phase 3 — legal validation. Responsible institutions approve a bounded rule set, use, version and reasons protocol through the appropriate legal and administrative instruments. Independent reviewers test authority, source fidelity, edge cases, data and prohibited outcomes. Any `[GAP]` that controls the result prevents progression.

20.11.6 Phase 4 — bounded public assistance and scale decision. A public service may explain the perimeter, collect an evidence inventory and route a user to the competent process. It should not issue a compliance badge or licence. Scale occurs only after measured reduction in error or burden, no material rights or security defect, demonstrable human override, working remedies, sustainable ownership and a reasoned Commission/sector decision under existing law.

20.11.7 The stop rules are as important as the phases. Code must never decide whether Parliament conferred a power; resolve an unresolved conflict between statutes; determine a contested legal character solely from a label; find dishonesty or liability; impose a sanction; freeze property; grant, refuse, suspend or revoke a licence; decide proportionality; dispose of an appeal; or prevent a court from examining legality. It may assemble the record, identify the question, calculate a formally determinate element, display alternatives and expose missing proof. The judgment and legal act remain with the authorised human institution.

20.11.8 This boundary is not hostility to technology. It is the condition for trustworthy technology in public law. Code supplies precision, reproducibility and the capacity to test implementation. Law supplies authority, rights, limits, reasons and remedy. Capital supplies capability and exposure: the resources to build systems, the incentives that may distort them, and the losses distributed when they fail. Intelligent order is achieved when each is made visible to the others without being allowed to impersonate them.

20.11.9 Pakistan’s contribution need not be the largest automated regulatory platform. It can be more important: a model of machine-legible administration in which the source is authenticated, drafts cannot masquerade as law, gaps stop false certainty, every branch is traceable, institutions retain their lawful competence, adverse decisions remain reasoned and reviewable, and correction improves both text and implementation. That is how a National Digital Masterplan can move toward machine-executable regulation without making regulation machine-sovereign.

-**Phase 0 — source integrity.** Establish authenticated source registers for the VAA, valid subordinate instruments and directly connected law. Assign provision identifiers, status, commencement, amendment and official-location metadata. Publicly separate operative, draft, historical and missing material. No executable case outcome is required.
-**Phase 1 — controlled research prototype.** Refactor the existing perimeter screen into a self-contained, reproducible package. Replace legal-conclusion checkboxes with human determination objects. Add missing-input, draft, gap, cross-regulator and source-change cases. Publish the rule map, limitations and test results as research. Success is faithful traceability and safe escalation, not approv
-**Phase 2 — institutional shadow pilot.** With PVARA and connected institutions’ approval, trained officers run the model alongside—not inside—the live process. It cannot affect an applicant.
